chunk_map.heading: Every task maps onto the same six phases

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent nobody can resolve breaks comprehension mid-deck. Chunk 1: 'them' (line 5, "The loops drawn across them all run the same shape") resolves to 'Six phases' one clause earlier in the same sentence; the six bold-led bullets (lines 9-14) each define their own term inline (Intent/Context/Work/Verification/Absorption/Outcome), no forward reference; the closer 'The phases are places' (line 16) resolves to the six just enumerated. Chunk 2: 'this territory' (line 20) resolves against chunk 0's title 'The whole map' (line 1) plus chunk 1's 'cycle'/'Six phases' (line 5) — same-file, earlier-chunk naming, not a forward pointer; 'it' (line 20, "before you see it drawn") resolves to 'a country' in the same sentence; 'here' (line 21, "Every move so far has lived here") resolves to 'The near half' stated at the start of the same bullet; 'there' (line 22, "The rest of the training goes there") resolves to 'The far half' stated at the start of the same bullet. No never-named, vague, or re-chunk-stranded referent anywhere in the body. Harm absent.

No pointer to another file by position ("the opening lecture said", "as file X showed") occurs anywhere in the body (raw lines 1-23). 'M1 was the first step into this territory' (line 20) names a module by its stable arc label, not another document by page position, and is scored under rule 3, not rule 2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead beat reference strands a student who goes looking for something that isn't there. Line 20 ('M1 was the first step into this territory, taken without the map on purpose... The first fix, the first rule, the first read of the context window') names M1 in general terms — the first, currently-shipping module of this training — not a specific exercise/lecture beat that a re-chunk could strand ('the catch on the missing PR'-style canonical failure). M1 exists and precedes this M2 opener per the training's own module order. No 'the X you did/saw' construction pointing at a beat that could go stale. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction ("take a guess before...") occurs anywhere in this container lecture; na_reason: no live-demo beat present.

Chunk 1 (lines 3-17) carries the lede, the full figure, six defined phases, and a places-not-pipeline closer — not a bare wait-state. Chunk 2 (lines 18-23) carries three self-carrying orientation bullets (M1 recap, near-half definition, far-half definition), each a complete standalone claim. Neither chunk is a single context-dependent bullet.

Header 'Every task maps onto the same six phases' (line 3) is confirmed by the chunk's own line 5 ('Every piece of agentic work maps onto the same cycle. Six phases.') and the six-bullet enumeration (lines 9-14) that follows — literally true summary. Header 'You are here' (line 18) is confirmed by the chunk's content: it places the reader relative to M1 (line 20) and names the near/far halves (lines 21-22) — the chunk does orient the reader, nothing contradicts the header.

Per sub-item, body lines 1-23 plus the figure's label text (raw line 7, the {{figure:map-engine}} expansion): (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction — none. (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples — none; the figure's short verb chains ('act · read the result · correct', 'run · let it fail · shape the verifier · re-run', 'read · judge · gate what ships · by hand for now') are mechanism lists of 3-4 items, not repeated sentence-opener/closer triples. (c) Self-grading superlatives — none ('one of the most useful' etc. does not occur). (d) Number + own retraction — 'Six phases' (line 5) is stated once, plainly, never hedged/walked back; not the retraction pattern. (e) Abstraction-noun stacks — none; phase definitions (lines 9-14) name concrete objects (files, rules, memory; tests, checks, reads, judges) rather than stacked abstractions. (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg — 'acts, reads the result, corrects, goes again' (line 11) and the figure's verb chains cited above: every leg is independently concrete (nothing answers 'what does this concretely mean?' with nothing). No cadence tic anywhere in the deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer/repo vocabulary lands where a room full of engineers cannot parse it. No repo-internal dialect term (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat-as-noun, mood-as-noun, Connections) appears anywhere in the body (lines 1-23) or in the figure's label text (raw line 7 expansion). The nine loop-strand names in the figure (THE CONTEXT LOOP, THE PLAN LOOP · CORE, THE SECURITY LOOP, THE PROTOTYPING LOOP, THE BUILD LOOP, THE AGENT'S OWN LOOP, THE CHECKING LOOP, THE COMPOUNDING LOOP, CROSSING THE WALL) are this training's own coined arc vocabulary (Field Guide pattern names), not maintainer-editorial dialect, and 'loop'/'compounding' are ordinary shop vocabulary for this audience regardless. Harm absent. (Whether any of these coined terms is used *before* the module that earns it is a check_writing.md §14/arc-vocabulary question, out of this class's lane — not scored here.)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: New rule since the prior instance (rule_inventory now lists 16 rules where the prior instance evaluated 15); evaluated fresh. (a) Doctrine restatement: none of the nine bullets re-announces a split/lens/law already stated earlier in this file or arc — the six phase definitions (lines 9-14) are each a first-time naming, and the near/far-half bullets (lines 21-22) are the first statement of that split in this file. (b) Self-referential design commentary: closest candidate is line 20, 'M1 was the first step into this territory, taken without the map on purpose' — this names a real design choice, but it stays inside because it is embedded in a sentence doing concrete orientation work (locating the student's actual M1 artifacts — 'the first fix, the first rule, the first read of the context window' — on the map) rather than standing alone as bare pedagogy-commentary like the rule's own bad examples ('You encounter the problems before the training names them'); it is four words, not a freestanding bullet, and it answers a real question the student would otherwise have (why didn't M1 have this map?). (line 22) is the closest candidate — it stays inside because it carries real sequencing information (the far half is not now) rather than restating the header or a stated '**The point:**' line; there is no koan closing a law here.
